evidence.note: Measured method distribution and per-method empty/pass rates during investigation — cost-to-pass awareness that can inform which methods to prioritize.

Wrote scaffolding in a clearly layered order: protocol plumbing (main.rs, jsonrpc.rs), lsp.rs, analyzer.rs (symbol model), resolver.rs, then per-handler files — a real layer hierarchy rather than a monolithic push.
First build then first test run then stdio initialize handshake test — treats 'protocol layer minimally works' as a concrete done-check before building on it.

Sustained method-by-method loop (selectionRange, call_hierarchy, references, documentHighlight, documentSymbol, hover, folding, implementation, semantic...), each isolated and re-verified with run_tests — one-at-a-time discipline with concrete checks across the whole horizon.
TodoWrite used to structure and update milestones at start, mid, and end, indicating maintained sub-goal tracking (though the sequencing rationale is not visibly cost/dependency-ordered).

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it identifies the main layers, builds them in a sensible protocol→parser→symbol-model→handlers order, tackles methods one at a time, and uses build/test/handshake runs as concrete done-checks. It approaches the level-8 anchor via pre-build cost-to-pass analysis (method distribution/empty rates) and layered handlers that build on a validated analyzer, but the method sequence reads more opportunistic (fix whatever's failing) than a deliberately dependency-and-cost-prioritized plan, and explicit per-milestone criteria aren't strongly evidenced. This places the observed behavior at a 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
